# Adapter: Witcher Gear Map

## In short

You used to push your markers with your own types (`WitcherGearWolf` and the rest) and draw them in your own map file. Your script keeps pushing the same pins; the art and tab come from calls:

```
CMFRegisterIcon("modWitcherGearMap", 'WitcherGearWolf', "img://icons/modcmfadapterwitchergearmap/gear.png");
CMFRegisterTint("modWitcherGearMap", 'WitcherGearWolf', 16736352);
CMFRegister("modWitcherGearMap", 8, 'wgm_gear', '', "[[map_category_wgm_gear]]", 8);
CMFRegister("modWitcherGearMap", 6, 'WitcherGear', '', "wgm_gear", 703);
```

Gear's pins use numeric ids (from 1464287232), so another mod reaches them by type or in `OnPinReady`, not by tag. The adapter is `source/adapters/witcher-gear-map`.

## The whole change, for its author

This note is for the author of Witcher Upgrade Gear Map (Nexus 14157). It shows what it takes for Gear Map's markers to appear on Conjunction Map Framework's (CMF) world map, using the adapter CMF ships as a proof of concept, [`source/adapters/witcher-gear-map/modCMFAdapterWitcherGearMap`](../../source/adapters/witcher-gear-map/modCMFAdapterWitcherGearMap/).

### Why your markers need anything at all

Only one `panel_worldmap.redswf` loads. When CMF is installed, CMF's map loads instead of Gear Map's, so the 26 frames you added to the pin sprite are not there. Your scripts keep running and keep sending markers named `WitcherGear`, `WitcherGearObtained`, `WitcherGearCat`, `WitcherGearObtainedCatRing` and so on. CMF's map receives them but has no art for those names.

CMF fixes that without a map file: a mod tells CMF, by name, which image to draw for a pin type, and CMF draws it.

### The quick change: ship one optional folder

Your existing mod does not change. Next to it you publish an optional "CMF support" folder. It is the adapter with your art in place of the placeholder:

```
Mods/
  modWitcherGearMapCMF/                         any folder name of yours, starting with "mod"
    README.txt
    content/texture.cache                       your icons, built by CMF's pack tool
    content/scripts/local/modwitchergearmapcmf_cmf.ws
```

The script is one `OnGameStarted` wrapper with one `CMFRegisterIcon` call per marker type you use, plus a `CMFRegisterTint` call where you want CMF to colour the art. Copy [the adapter's script](../../source/adapters/witcher-gear-map/modCMFAdapterWitcherGearMap/content/scripts/local/modcmfadapterwitchergearmap_cmf.ws), then replace the provider id `modCMFAdapterWitcherGearMap` with your folder name, everywhere it appears. That folder name is your provider id.

It stays a separate folder because a CMF call fails to compile when CMF is not installed. Players without CMF install your mod as today; players with CMF add the folder.

### Where your art goes

1. Export your marker art as square PNGs, 96 x 96 recommended, transparent background, with the outer 4 pixels left empty. The rules are in the [icon pack guide](Getting-Started.md#4-make-your-art).
2. Put them in the folder's `art/`. Either:
   - **keep the adapter's four names**, `gear.png`, `gear_obtained.png`, `gear_ring.png` and `gear_obtained_ring.png`, and let CMF's tints colour them by school. Paint the parts that should take the school colour white or light, because a tint multiplies; or
   - **give each type its own image**, for example `art/witchergearobtainedcatring.png`, point that type's `CMFRegisterIcon` at it, and delete its `CMFRegisterTint` line.
3. Run `python tools/cmf_pack.py build path/to/modWitcherGearMapCMF --out path/to/new-folder` from the CMF repository. It cooks your PNGs into the folder's own `texture.cache` and writes the `Mods` folder to ship. It warns that names like `WitcherGear` are not 5.01 pin types. That is expected, because they are yours.

The image path for `art/<name>.png` is `img://icons/<your folder in lower case>/<name>.png`.

### What already works, and what does not yet

Works through CMF with no change from you: every marker, its position, its title, the tooltip with each diagram's status and the location hint, Gear Map's options (show, discovered only, hide obtained, icon style, school, tier, notify, debug), and the learned-state switch to the obtained art.

**Your "Witcher Gear" filter category, under API version 2.** API version 2 lets a mod add legend rows and filter tabs as data, with the generic `CMFRegister` call (property ids 6, 7 and 8). The adapter registers your own names, so your text shows with no change from you:

```
if (CMFHasProperty(8))
{
	CMFRegister("modCMFAdapterWitcherGearMap", 8, 'wgm_gear', '', "[[map_category_wgm_gear]]", 8);
	CMFRegister("modCMFAdapterWitcherGearMap", 6, 'WitcherGear', '', "wgm_gear", 703);
	CMFRegister("modCMFAdapterWitcherGearMap", 7, 'WitcherGear', '', "[[wgm_label]]", 0);
}
```

That gives a "Witcher Gear" tab after the game's tabs, with your row in it at 703. The row is also listed under Default and All, as in your own map file. It is named "Witcher Gear" from your `wgm_label`, not after the first marker. The `CMFHasProperty(8)` guard keeps the script compiling on API version 1, which skips the block. Under API version 2, hiding the row under All hides every one of your 26 types, not only plain `WitcherGear` markers. In your own map file, hiding it there misses the other 25 types. This passed in game in the API version 2 launch (2026-10-20). A CMF support folder of your own carries the same block with your folder name as the provider.

Not yet under CMF:

- **Under API version 1, no filter category.** CMF's map then lists your markers only under All, in a row named after the first marker's title.
- **The legend row does not follow the icon style.** All your markers share one legend row, because they share `filteredType` `WitcherGear`. That row takes the `WitcherGear` image, so the ring and school colour show on markers only. Until a pending CMF core change lands, the row can also pick up the first marker's school colour. After it, the row's colour comes only from a claim on `WitcherGear`. A CMF support folder of your own can register a legend image per style with `CMFRegisterLegendIcon(..., 'WitcherGear', ...)` after reading your `wgm_IconStyle` setting.
- **Marker clicks** do what any non-quest pin does on the map. Gear Map uses no click action today.
- **The combined Gear and Gwent map file** is not needed under CMF. CMF's map loads instead, and each mod's markers come through its own CMF support folder.

### One thing we noticed in Gear Map 1.0.1

This happens with or without CMF. On a fresh install, the School, Tier and Icon style options have no stored value until the player changes them once. `GetVarValue` then returns `"-1"`, not `""`, so `wgm_InitConfig` does not store the defaults. The school filter then drops every marker, and the map shows "0 locations" while the menu shows "All". Treating `"-1"` like `""` in `wgm_InitConfig` would fix it.

### Can CMF do this without the author?

Yes, and that is what the adapter is. It uses the same names your mod already sends and copies none of your code or art. Its placeholder art is the adapter's own, in its `texture.cache`; CMF itself carries none. It is a stand-in until you publish your own CMF support folder, which loads your art the same way.
